correctness.rationale: Tame inertia in degree three acts by 3-cycles, and killing the normal subgroup generated by inertia would give an étale cover of the geometric projective line, so the geometric deck group is C₃. It acts faithfully on the hyperelliptic line. In the reduced Artin–Schreier equation the genus permits only pole orders (5), (3,1), or (1,1,1). At a fixed pole the primitive cube-root tangent multiplier forces the highest odd pole order to be divisible by three: a coboundary cannot supply a competing highest pole of odd order. The first two types are thus impossible. The unique cyclic permutation of three simple poles up to inversion has a one-dimensional invariant principal-part space, which descends under Frobenius; its one nonzero F₂-vector gives two constant twists per divisor. Checking the divisor stabilizers identifies the twists in the split and mixed cases, but not in the cubic case. The displayed functions are invariant under the stated order-three maps; adjoining y base-changes their degree-three covers by the separable quadratic Artin–Schreier map. The two field extensions have coprime degrees, so the degree is still three. The preimage of the pole C₃ in the curve automorphism group is a central extension of C₃ by the hyperelliptic C₂ and has a unique C₃ subgroup. This gives target-coordinate uniqueness over F₂. The nonpole critical x-values of the split and cubic functions are ω,ω² and their function values are ω²,ω; those of the mixed function are 0,1 with values 1,0. All poles are simple and infinity for the cubic functions has local degree one. Pulling back the critical values through T²+T gives the displayed quartics; the polynomial with constant one has no roots even in F₄ and hence is irreducible. Counting the unique points at rational poles and two or zero elsewhere by trace gives the four point-count pairs. The degree-one and degree-two exclusions follow from genus and wild hyperelliptic ramification.
residual_risks: Correctness concerns the geometric inertia indices and F₂-isomorphisms; the mixed cover's geometric cyclic deck generators are not all defined over F₂. No general classification for higher tame degrees or formal certificate asserted.

evidence: CNP's 5q−6 count for the four F₂ twists at q=2 and the group C₂×S₃ cover the model and automorphism part. General existence of tame maps does not prescribe a minimizing degree or these four branch values.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A C₃ subgroup in the known automorphism group gives the geometric cyclic quotient, and the monodromy criterion identifies it as the only possible tame pencil. Those structural facts alone do not describe how Frobenius permutes its four branch values.

evidence: C₂×S₃ has a unique C₃, so geometric cyclicity makes uniqueness a direct application. For the quartic branch comparison, the rational-function critical values must be lifted through the degree-two target relation T²+T, giving values over F₁₆ in three cases and over F₄ in the mixed case.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The exact branch arithmetic is an extra invariant computation of the cubic cover. It is neither a restatement of the model/twist count nor a recoding of the hyperelliptic pole table; the needed critical-value or equivalent Frobenius calculation is additional even though the equations determine it.

In a reduced degree-four divisor, zero rational points still allows (4) or (2,2) without more information. The inspected census does not give that distinction as a cubic branch datum.

originality.rationale: The underlying model list, twists and geometric automorphism groups are known, and quotient uniqueness substantially uses that known structure. The supported distinct finding is the arithmetic branch classification of the unique tame cubic pencil, not the enumeration of the curves. The strongest inspected table covers the four equations and counts rational totally ramified fibres of their degree-three rulings but not the remaining branch degrees. The older classification concerns the splitting of the hyperelliptic poles, not the branch splitting of this cubic quotient.
residual_risks: Priority against other characteristic-two Hurwitz or explicit quotient computations is not settled. The known enumeration, rational-branch count and automorphism-based uniqueness are not claimed as separate original results.

value.rationale: Branch Frobenius is an intrinsic arithmetic invariant here because the tame cubic pencil is unique over F₂. The full spectrum says which field extensions first see individual branch values, including the irreducible quartic case not recorded by a rational-fibre count. This is useful in comparing small-characteristic covers and their twists, not merely a new enumeration of familiar curves.
residual_risks: Value is for the natural degree-three branch invariant, not for claims about minimal tame degrees of the other curves beyond the lower bound, or for a classification of covers of higher degrees.
